svg.title: Segment Tree with Lazy Propagation and Trie Prefix Tree Traversal
svg.desc: Animated step-by-step visualization of Segment Tree range addition add([0..3], +5) storing a deferred lazy tag at [0..3], followed by pushDown on demand during query([2..3]), paired with a Trie prefix walk inserting and matching 'cat', 'car', and 'cart' in O(L) time.
svg.text: Deferred pushDown() Range Updates in 4n Slots (O(log n) Update + Query) vs O(L) Shared-Prefix Character Walk
1. Segment Tree: Range Update + Lazy pushDown

g.text: Node [0..3] lies fully inside update range. Update sum += 4*5 = 20,
set lazy[node] += 5, and return IMMEDIATELY without visiting children!
Step 3: Exact Hit at [2..3] -> Returns sum = 10 in O(log n)!
Individual leaf nodes 0, 1, 2, 3 were never visited yet remain consistent
because deferred tags wait until a query needs finer granularity.

svg.text: 1. Handles non-invertible monoids (RMQ min/max, GCD, matrix product).
2. Lazy propagation guarantees O(log n) worst-case range updates & queries.
3. Allocate 4 * n slots to cover arbitrary non-power-of-two array sizes safely.
Animated prefix walk for query/insert("cart") sharing "ca-" & "car":

g.text: Char 0: Start at Root -> lookup edge 'c'
O(1) array/map child transition per character.
Char 1: 'c' -> node "c" (shared by cat, car, cart)
Zero duplicate prefix allocation across 3 stored words.
Prefix search startsWith("ca") resolves in 2 steps!
Prefix "car" is itself a complete word AND continues via 't'.
Finished in 4 steps = O(L), completely independent of dictionary size N.

svg.text: Fixed 26-slot arrays give O(1) transitions; use hash map / Radix Tree to compress sparse nodes.
Exact query hit / isWordEnd(*) terminal node
Segment Tree achieves O(log n) worst-case range queries and range updates; Trie achieves O(L) prefix & autocomplete lookup regardless of word count N.
